tagline: Over the Height of Land and down among the trout lakes.
intro: Route 17 starts just north of Byron and climbs to the Height of Land, which looks out over the Rangeley Lakes region, then follows the western shore of Rangeley Lake to Oquossoc. From there the byway turns east to Rangeley and takes Route 4 south to Smalls Falls on the Sandy River. The Appalachian Trail crosses both Route 17 and Route 4.
Pioneers and woodsmen settled the country in the early 1800s. In the 1860s word got out about brook trout of 10 and 12 pounds, and the region became a resort. Herbert Hoover was among the anglers.

moments.title: Height of Land
moments.text: A viewpoint on Route 17 over the lakes, where on summer weekends byway ambassadors stand ready to tell travelers where to find a trail, or a moose.

moments.title: Rangeley
moments.text: Squire James Rangeley came in 1825 to build an English-style estate, stayed 15 years and moved to Portland. A sign in town puts it halfway between the Equator and the North Pole.

moments.title: Smalls Falls
moments.text: From a rest area on Route 4, the Sandy River comes down 54 feet in a slide, a waterfall, a horsetail and a short cascade, with pools between.
